auditor.independence: I translated none of these keys, ran no part of the S17c draft audit and integrated nothing; in this session I re-derived every check from the bytes myself (parent prefix, draft equality, key set, ICU parse and per-arm placeholders, format, glossary census), reading the prior records only after forming my own per-key judgment.

findings.note: EN 'Reconnect' (9 chars, one word) -> 'دوبارہ منسلک کریں' (17, three words); the twin ui.chat.run_details.mcp.control.reload is the same shape, 'Reload' (6) -> 'دوبارہ لوڈ کریں' (15). Urdu has no one-word verb here and both renderings are fixed by the corpus (mcp_key.save 'محفوظ کریں اور دوبارہ منسلک کریں'; ui.browser.chrome.reload 'دوبارہ لوڈ کریں'), so I propose no divergent shorter form. Width read from the components, not from pixels: the shared Button is `whitespace-nowrap shrink-0` (shared/components/ui/button.tsx:132-133) and every row that holds these labels is `flex flex-wrap` (mcp-auth-dialog.tsx:436/490/532; run-detail-mcp.tsx), so an over-wide label wraps to a second line and costs height, never text — and a pre-existing 38-char words remedy (mcp.credentials_in_settings, 'اس سرور کی اسناد ترتیبات میں منظم کریں') already renders on the same action line, so 15-17 chars are within existing practice. Non-gating; still worth one rendered frame, because the sign-in dialog's failure footer now asks one row to hold Grant account access (19) + Enter API key (17) + دوبارہ منسلک کریں (17) together.

EN 'Cancelling…' -> 'منسوخی جاری ہے…', while the two sibling button labels of the same state in this namespace read 'منسوخ ہو رہی ہے…' (wake.cancelling, wake_cancel.cancelling) and monitor_cancel.stopping reads 'روکی جا رہی ہے…'. One panel, two shapes for one button state. Both are grammatical, and the noun form has a real virtue: it asserts no gender for جاب (no corpus string agrees an adjective with جاب; 'جاب کی منسوخی' agrees with منسوخی, not with جاب). Keep as-is unless the sibling labels are being unified anyway; if so, 'منسوخ ہو رہی ہے…' is the shape to converge on.
